question: Should a descendant completion be durably classified as `delivered` when an internal requester demonstrably consumes it, even if the requester's final outward delivery later fails?
rationale: This is a durable lifecycle and user-delivery contract, not a mechanical implementation detail: it changes what persisted `delivered` means for cleanup, restoration, and downstream consumers.

options.title: Treat requester consumption as delivery credit
options.body: Accept the proposed internal-consumption contract, but require focused live upgrade/restart proof and a narrow branch limited to that contract.

options.title: Keep delivered user-visible only
options.body: Retain the existing meaning of `delivered` and introduce a distinct requester-consumed state or follow-up path if the information is still needed.

options.title: Defer to durable inbox design
options.body: Pause this narrow accounting change until the broader completion-delivery persistence design is settled in the existing planning work.

recommendation.title: Treat requester consumption as delivery credit
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed internal-consumption contract, but require focused live upgrade/restart proof and a narrow branch limited to that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged descendant-announcement design is the closest established ownership signal for the completion-consumption boundary.
